races.name: Teenage Cancer Trust Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Recon Mission
runners_data.note: A 10-year-old veteran hold-up operator for Tony Carroll who prefers to be produced late; George Downing takes the ride but just 5 wins and one place from 15 runs on similar going underlines a modest conversion rate, and at 46 days off there is no freshness angle to exploit.|
runners_data.comment: Recon Mission has placed second and third in recent starts and shapes as a clear threat here, with experience over today's trip and going working in his favour; the worry is that he's been winless in his last five starts and hasn't run for 46 days.

runners_data.name: Diomed Spirit
runners_data.note: Charles Gordon's six-year-old has back-to-back placings at 5f on good ground in his recent history (2nd, 3rd) and Chris Gordon's yard is in 0/0 form over the last 14 days, so there is no live stable spark here; his style leaves him dependent on the pace collapsing, which this shape is unlikely to provide.|
runners_data.comment: Diomed Spirit arrives as the top-rated runner in the field, and his second last time out — off a 39-day break carrying 135 lb from stall one — marks him as a genuine threat with distance and going experience in the book; the risk is that he's yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Dreambird Dolly
runners_data.note: Strong recent form figures — a win and multiple places including two seconds on good ground at 5f — mark Dreambird Dolly as the most in-form runner in the field; Donagh Murphy (7) claims a useful allowance and the tongue-tie is familiar headgear, though her true style is hold-up and she will need to press closer than usual to be dangerous in this pace-controlled shape.|
runners_data.comment: Dreambird Dolly has experience of today's trip and going, and consecutive runner-up finishes show she's in decent nick, but ranked sixth of seven on our figures she faces a stiff task at the weights carrying 134 lb from stall six.

runners_data.name: Stapleford Park
runners_data.note: Consistent at 5-6f on standard going but without a win in the last six runs, and 109 days off the track is the longest absence in the field; James Glennon (7) is an apprentice booking that may reflect confidence rather than a betting move, and the horse's natural hold-up tendency means he will be sat off a slow-ish gallop unless he breaks well and the connections push him forward.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and returning after 109 days off, Stapleford Park does have experience over today's trip and a second two starts back to suggest some ability, though sevenths at two of his last four outings are hard to ignore from stall two carrying 134 lb.

runners_data.name: Washington Heir
runners_data.note: Recorded a recent win at 6f on good ground with William Carson and carries live claims for Tony Carroll's yard (4/40 T14); his running style is naturally hold-up but his last-five record shows he can place himself closer when the race demands it, and the drop to OR 50 after that win gives him a competitive weight.|
runners_data.comment: Washington Heir showed a win two starts back, and that third last time out keeps him lightly respected, but he ranks last on our figures in a field of seven and his official mark of 50 leaves little margin — hard to fancy at the weights.

runners_data.name: Reporter
runners_data.note: Wears a hood today and Simon Hodgson's 0/2 14-day record is quiet; a genuine hold-up type who has finished outside the frame in his last two starts, and while his 5f good-ground form includes a win, the redistribution to midfield rather than his preferred rear position means William Carver faces a tactical puzzle to find a clear run.|

runners_data.name: Hakin Adraar
runners_data.note: Martin Dunne's three-year-old is the only horse in the race willing to make the running and benefits enormously from that unchallenged position; just eight days since his last run suggests fitness, but his form in last five starts shows no win at 5-7f on any going — his best chance is that the controllable pace proves kinder than his bare figures suggest.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Hakin Adraar nevertheless brings strong fitness credentials just eight days since his last outing, has experience of today's trip and conditions, and steps up on his official mark on our figures — drawn four carrying 127 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Hakin Adraar is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner 5½f Brighton handicap and, with no rival willing or able to press him hard from the gates, he is set to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on good-to-firm ground. The remaining six runners — Recon Mission, Diomed Spirit, Dreambird Dolly, Stapleford Park, Washington Heir, and Reporter — are all hold-up types by nature, meaning the field will stack up behind a single pace-setter rather than fragment into a true contest of speeds. Because Hakin Adraar faces zero pressure on the front end, he is likely to bowl along at a rhythm that suits his stamina rather than expose it, making it very hard for genuine closers to generate the momentum they need over this sharp trip. This race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently or at least in close attendance early, since the absence of a true pace duel on a flat, right-handed track that does not naturally stretch out a field means late closers will find the ground cut from under their challenge. Several runners are redistributed in the map because the field contains far more hold-up types than the shape can accommodate at the rear; Dreambird Dolly, Washington Heir, and Stapleford Park are the most likely of these to push forward and secure a closer position to the pace than their natural style suggests.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hakin Adraar Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Hakin Adraar bowls clear from the gates and no rival is willing to commit early, he sets a gallop entirely on his own terms and the hold-up pack is left chasing.
scenarios.body: Hakin Adraar dictates every yard of the race, the field strings out behind him on a sound surface, and the gap he builds is never fully bridged; horses with the ability to travel closer to the leader — notably Dreambird Dolly or Washington Heir if they push up — have the best chance of catching him late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Pace Catches Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is just quick enough to stretch Hakin Adraar in the final furlong, the best of the hold-up horses — those who have managed to sit closer than their natural style — close him down.
scenarios.body: Dreambird Dolly's strong course-form on good going (13/15 sim-going, 1W7P at the trip) and Washington Heir's recent win form give them the profile to reel in a tying leader; this shape rewards the sharpest finisher who has maintained contact.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Late Run
scenarios.trigger: If Hakin Adraar over-extends himself on good-to-firm ground and ties up in the final 100 yards, the closers who have settled deepest — Recon Mission or Diomed Spirit — can sweep past.
scenarios.body: Brighton's undulations can catch out front-runners who have gone too hard in the back end, and both Recon Mission and Diomed Spirit have the course-distance profile to benefit from a stamina-based finish; this remains a lower-probability outcome given the controlled nature of the expected pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrambled Midfield Melee
scenarios.trigger: If several redistributed hold-up types push forward simultaneously and create unexpected crowding and interference in the early stages, the race degenerates into a scrappy contest with no single leader dominant.
scenarios.body: Reporter or Stapleford Park, given their wider draw angles, could find daylight in the chaos; however this scenario is markedly discounted because most of these horses will ultimately settle rather than fight for position in a small field.

watchPoints.text: Hakin Adraar's ability to control tempo entirely without a challenge is the single biggest race factor — watch whether he is allowed to bowl clear in the first furlong or whether any rival breaks sharply and forces him into a faster gallop than intended.

Dreambird Dolly and Washington Heir are natural hold-up horses who may push forward to cover the pace; if both attempt to do so simultaneously they risk burning each other's energy in the first two furlongs, undermining both chances.

Stapleford Park's 109-day absence is the longest in the field — watch in the paddock and early in the race for any signs of rustiness or greenness that could cause interference in the compressed, single-pace shape this race is likely to produce.

Reporter wears a hood for the first time or as a routine aid — watch at the start whether the headgear has a calming or unsettling effect, as a slowly-away hold-up type in a race with only one pace-setter has very little room to recover lost ground over 5½f.|

races.name: JenningsBet In Portsmouth EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Bands C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)
JenningsBet UK's Largest Independent Bookmaker Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Celebrating Ethel
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll handler with four winners from 40 runners in 14 days; wears a hood and returns just two days after her last run, but her true racing style is rear-of-field and she has been pushed into a midfield berth she won't naturally occupy — zero wins and zero places from five runs on similar Good ground compounds the concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Celebrating Ethel nevertheless ran fourth last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, while our rating puts her second among six — the risk is the quick two-day turnaround under a stiff 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Dogged
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old asked to front-run despite being a natural hold-up horse, wearing blinkers on a one-day turnaround for Carroll; his three places from 11 runs on Good going show he handles the surface, but setting fractions from the lead is an unfamiliar ask and he is likely to be caught late if he over-extends.
runners_data.comment: Placed last time out and a second four starts back, Dogged has experience over today's trip and conditions, and his 48 rating edges his official mark — the main risk is he runs just one day after his latest start.

runners_data.name: Fitzmaurice
runners_data.note: Four-year-old who has never run beyond 8f in his last five starts, stepping up to 1m2f on a track that will test his stamina; a true hold-up horse placed in midfield for this analysis, his form figures of 768785 and zero wins or places on Good ground make him an outsider whose chance depends on finding extra at a trip he is unproven at.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with finishes of fifth, eighth, seventh, eighth, sixth and seventh telling a consistent tale of mid-to-tail-of-field efforts, Fitzmaurice is hard to fancy ranked last of six on our figures, though he has run over today's going and returns on a handy 14-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Myna
runners_data.note: The one horse correctly mapped at the rear who owns genuine course-and-distance credentials — a win at 10f on Good ground and three placed efforts in similar conditions for Carroll make this the horse most naturally suited to Brighton's contours and today's race shape; George Downing takes the ride.
runners_data.comment: Myna has been knocking at the door in his last two starts — a second two runs back and a third last time out — and has experience of today's trip and going. Carrying 135 lb from stall six, he holds the strongest rating in the field and returns on a sharp 17-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Outrace
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse who fades in the finish, carrying a style-fit discount after being placed in midfield rather than his natural hold-up position; Richard Hannon's runner has recorded four last-place finishes from his last five starts on similar surfaces, and the fade warning makes him a significant risk even if the pace were to collapse.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Outrace has struggled for consistency and sits fifth of six on our figures, making him hard to fancy at the weights; he does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and a return 13 days ago keeps him fit.

runners_data.name: Thundering Breeze
runners_data.note: David Probert takes the ride for Gary & Josh Moore, who have just one winner from 19 runners over the past fortnight; the big question is fitness after 176 days off, but his prior form at 10f–11f on Soft suggests he handles the step in trip, and a clean run from a handy position gives him each-way claims if freshness proves a positive.
runners_data.comment: Thundering Breeze has placed — a second three starts back and a third five starts back — and has run over today's trip and going, giving her every chance to threaten here; the main risk is a 176-day absence that leaves fitness the key question.

races.paceDynamic: Dogged is the only confirmed pace-setter in this six-runner field and, redistributed from his natural hold-up role, he will be asked to make the running — creating a steady, uncontested gallop on Good to Firm ground over Brighton's undulating 1m2f. With Dogged setting a sustainable tempo from the front, the race is unlikely to be run at a searching pace, which typically hands an advantage to horses who can travel prominently and quicken once the hill is crested rather than those waiting furthest back. Myna is the standout natural hold-up type with genuine course-and-distance form at this track and trip, and a race run at a controlled pace over Brighton's unique contours suits a horse who can pick up in the straight. Thundering Breeze returns from a 176-day absence and carries fitness doubt, while the three redistributed midfield types — Outrace, Fitzmaurice, and Celebrating Ethel — are all true hold-up horses unable to secure their natural rear position, meaning their tactical options are compressed. This race shape favours genuine hold-up horses who can travel comfortably in mid-to-rear and produce a late effort down Brighton's long run-in, with Myna best placed to exploit Dogged's manufactured lead.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dogged Dictates, Myna Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Dogged secures the lead without any serious pressure and sets a fair but manageable gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Dogged rolls along in front unchallenged, keeping the pace honest enough that closers remain in contention, but Myna — the one genuine hold-up horse mapped correctly at the rear — produces a sustained run to reel him in entering the final furlong. Brighton's finishing straight rewards horses who travel well and pick up once balanced, and Myna's course-and-distance record (1W3P in recent 10f Good ground) fits this template precisely.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Thundering Breeze Freshness Factor
scenarios.trigger: If Thundering Breeze's 176-day layoff masks peak fitness that allows him to track Dogged and outstay the field up the hill.
scenarios.body: A fresh horse trained by Gary & Josh Moore occasionally returns sharper than expected, and Thundering Breeze's prior placed form over 10f on similar ground gives him the profile to travel in second and collar Dogged late. If he handles the absence and the undulations, his stamina at this trip over Brighton's specific demands could prove the decisive factor.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Compressed Field, Redistributed Types Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up horses forced into midfield — Outrace, Fitzmaurice, or Celebrating Ethel — find their stride despite racing out of role and make late headway.
scenarios.body: With several horses occupying closer positions than natural, one of the redistributed midfield runners could benefit if the pace is truly crawling and the race turns into a sprint-finish from 2f out. However, all three carry STYLE_FIT discounts of 0.91–0.92 and poor recent form figures, making this scenario reliant on a significant departure from expected race shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Dawdle Turns Tactical
scenarios.trigger: If Dogged's manufactured lead produces an extremely slow early pace that collapses into a mass sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A race devoid of genuine pace pressure can occasionally produce a bunched finish where class and draw advantages are neutralised, and any runner able to quicken off a slow tempo could outgun the others in the final furlong. Given the all-level 135lb weights and compressed OR band (44–48), this scenario is possible but unlikely to separate the field decisively.

watchPoints.text: Dogged's ability to control fractions from the front will define the race shape — watch whether William Carson allows him to bowl along or whether he attempts to hold him up despite the front-running instruction, as any reluctance in the early stages could cause the field to bunch dangerously.

Thundering Breeze is 176 days off the track and any sign of greenness or sluggishness leaving the stalls would immediately undermine his chance of tracking Dogged into a prominent position where Probert will want him to be.

Outrace is explicitly flagged as a horse who fades in the finish and carries a compressed midfield position that is not his natural role — if he is ridden aggressively early to justify that map position, he risks emptying well before the line and interfering with others in a six-runner field.

With all six runners carrying identical 135lb weights and ORs within a four-pound band (44–48), any significant market moves at the track for Myna or Thundering Breeze are worth noting as the key market signal in a wide-open class race.

races.name: Harry Bloom Memorial "Brighton Bullet" Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: The Quiet Gent
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator returning after 295 days off — the lengthy break is the dominant concern; David Probert fits well but the horse will need everything to go right late over Brighton's short straight, tracking from the rear as is his nature.
runners_data.comment: After a promising third and second in recent starts, The Quiet Gent has experience over today's trip and going, and his rating of 87 marks him out as a lively threat from stall five — though 295 days off the track and a winless recent run of five starts make fitness the key question.

runners_data.name: Marcellinus
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent performer at 6f on good ground with four places from five runs at this trip; Tom Dascombe's yard is cold at 0/12 over the last 14 days but Donagh Murphy's 7lb claim keeps the weight competitive and he has the profile to secure the berth directly behind Grey Horizon.
runners_data.comment: Marcellinus catches the eye with a second two starts back and a winner four starts back, and his consistent recent profile marks him out as the one to beat here. He has run over today's trip and going before, and our rating of 94 heads the field, though the 41-day absence is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Tenbob Tommy
runners_data.note: Won twice at 6f on good ground recently and clearly thrives on this surface; 116 days off is a mild flag but Sheena West has only two runners in the 14-day window suggesting a freshener rather than a campaign issue, and he is dangerous if he translates that form from a prominent pitch.
runners_data.comment: Tenbob Tommy has winning form in his last two starts but hasn't run in 116 days, and that fitness query is the key unknown; he has experience over today's trip and going, and carries 138 lb from stall 4.

runners_data.name: Lequinto
runners_data.note: Reliable hold-up type who has won twice and placed three times from five runs at 6f on good ground — the going stats here are as strong as any runner in the field; Tony Carroll's yard is among the most active over the period and William Carson knows this course.
runners_data.comment: Lequinto has run over today's trip and going, and his recent form reads well — a winner two starts back and second last time out — though he carries 138 lb from stall seven and our rating of 78 ranks him seventh of ten.

runners_data.name: Bona Fortuna
runners_data.note: 309 days off the track is a sharp concern regardless of the solid each-way form on good ground at 5-6f; the tongue-tie is retained but Michael Appleby will need this to be a fitness spin before getting sharper, making the lengthy absence hard to dismiss.
runners_data.comment: Bona Fortuna arrives winless in his last five but has rattled up three seconds in recent starts, and experience over today's trip and ground gives him a live chance from stall one; the concern is a 309-day absence alongside a trainer firing at just 3% lately.

runners_data.name: Grey Horizon
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who won last time at 6f on good ground and has course form in the book; visor is retained, Christian Howarth's 3lb claim softens the weight, and the race hinges on whether he gets a solo lead — if he does, his rivals must come and find him.
runners_data.comment: Grey Horizon arrives on decent recent form — a winner last time out and a second two starts back — but his speed rating of 72 trails the field, and ranked eighth of ten on our figures, he faces a stiff task at 135 lb from stall six.

runners_data.name: Cayman Tai
runners_data.note: True hold-up type who ran just 13 days ago — the quick turnaround is noted but Richard Hannon's yard is in strong form at 10/59; the horse has limited 6f experience, most runs coming over 5f, and that step up in trip is an open question at this level.
runners_data.comment: Cayman Tai arrives in solid nick on 13 days' rest, and with experience of today's trip and going under his belt, his third two starts back underlines his consistency — though that fifth last time out suggests he'll need to find improvement to land the spoils from stall nine carrying 134 lb.

runners_data.name: U S S Charleston
runners_data.note: Ran only eight days ago and returned a win at 5f on soft; the slight step up to 6f on much quicker ground is a double query, and Connor Planas is an apprentice with limited exposure at this track — interesting if conditions suit but hard to rely on with those flags in play.
runners_data.comment: Ran second last time out in fair recent form, with one win in his last six starts; U S S Charleston has experience of today's trip and going, and at 132 lb from stall 3, his rating of 83 ranks him fifth of ten, with a bit to find.

runners_data.name: Ancient Times
runners_data.note: Strong recent record at 6f on good ground with two wins and a place from nine runs in similar conditions; genuinely a prominent racer by nature, he has been pushed into the midfield allocation because the field is saturated with horses wanting that position, meaning he may have to race a touch further back than ideal — temper expectations accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Three unplaced efforts punctuate his recent record, and he sits last on our figures among ten rivals — hard to fancy at the weights. The winning effort two starts back and a runner-up last time at least show he retains ability, and he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Duskaura
runners_data.note: Won last time at 6f on good ground and clearly handles the conditions; a natural hold-up horse by inclination who has been mapped to midfield simply because the rear is congested with similar types in this field — she may find her rhythm closer than usual, but Myla Coppins' 5lb claim on a 3-year-old is a positive if traffic clears.
runners_data.comment: Ranked ninth of ten on our figures, Duskaura has been largely out of the mix in recent starts — a sixth, sixth, fourth, seventh before winning last time out — making that latest victory hard to read with confidence. Has run over today's trip and going, and 13 days' rest is no concern.

races.paceDynamic: Grey Horizon is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will stride into an uncontested position from the gates and control tempo on his own terms over Brighton's 6f. The prominent cluster — Marcellinus, Tenbob Tommy, Bona Fortuna, and U S S Charleston — will jostle for the positions immediately behind him, creating meaningful traffic congestion between the 3f and 2f poles that threatens to trap several of those rivals at a critical moment. Hold-up horses The Quiet Gent, Lequinto, Cayman Tai, and Duskaura will be threading through that mess from off the pace in the straight. The field contains more prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — Marcellinus and Tenbob Tommy, both proven at 6f on good ground, are best placed to actually secure the cover they need, while Ancient Times and Duskaura are redistibuted away from their preferred positions and must be assessed with that constraint in mind. A controlled, honest gallop set by a single front-runner with a prominent pack behind favours the horses best positioned to travel into that pace without burning energy — prominent types who are comfortable at 6f on good-to-firm and have tactical flexibility to pick a path at the two-pole.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Grey Horizon Dictates Solo
scenarios.trigger: If Grey Horizon immediately opens a clear lead and the prominent pack settles without forcing a quicker tempo.
scenarios.body: Grey Horizon sets a measured pace with no pressure, turns for home with a decisive advantage, and his rivals burn energy fighting traffic rather than chasing him; his recent win at 6f on good ground confirms he can sustain this to the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Battle Upends Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Marcellinus or Tenbob Tommy refuses to settle and forces Grey Horizon to race harder than intended through the first 3f.
scenarios.body: A contested early pace makes the race genuinely truly-run, flattening Grey Horizon late and giving hold-up types a stronger late wind to exploit; Lequinto's consistent 6f good-ground form and Cayman Tai's willingness to come from off a pace make them natural beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Clears, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent scrimmage between 3f-2f causes interference and opens a clean late lane on the stands rail.
scenarios.body: The Quiet Gent and Lequinto, both positioned furthest back, find a gap in the final furlong and pick off tiring horses who burned energy in the early barging; Brighton's short straight limits this scenario unless the split appears early.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Scrambles the Field
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent runners contest the early lead hard, causing a rapid pace collapse that hands an unexpected result to a midfield drifter.
scenarios.body: Ancient Times, though shown in midfield due to redistribution rather than natural style, could benefit if confusion allows him to slot into an uncontested prominent pitch at a moderate tempo; Bona Fortuna, returning from 309 days off but proven in good-ground conditions at 6f, is a marginal lottery pick.

watchPoints.text: Grey Horizon's early position is the race — if any of Marcellinus, Tenbob Tommy, or U S S Charleston attempts to press him from the gates, the entire race shape accelerates and his chance deteriorates sharply.

Traffic congestion between the 3f-2f markers is near-certain with Marcellinus, Tenbob Tommy, Bona Fortuna, and U S S Charleston all seeking the same berths — horses on the inner rail could be severely hampered at a decisive moment.

Lequinto's connections (Tony Carroll, dual runner in the race with Duskaura) should be watched in the market — if either runner is heavily supported late, it could signal stable confidence in going conditions that suit both animals' strong good-ground profiles.

Bona Fortuna's return from 309 days is a market watch — a significant move at the off would suggest Appleby has done serious home work and the horse is primed despite the long absence; without that move, the break is too large to dismiss.

Brighton's 6f is a genuinely flat, straight track with a short run-in that rewards horses already in contention at the 2f pole — any hold-up horse who has not yet begun to make ground by the time the field straightens is almost certainly out of the race.

races.name: Bet In Over 200 Shops Nationwide With JenningsBet Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Dragon God
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for Tony Carroll who won over 5f on good ground five days ago — the step back up to 6f is a question but recent sharp form and Charles Bishop in the saddle are positives; sits naturally at the rear and will need the pace to be genuine to reel in a leader.
runners_data.comment: Dragon God won last time out and has experience of today's trip and going, making him a genuine threat from stall 4 carrying 138 lb; the concern is he was only fifth and sixth in two of his last six starts, suggesting consistency could be tested.

runners_data.name: Mart
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner here and will get every opportunity to dictate from the gates; Darragh Keenan takes over and the trainer has had no winners from three runners in the past 14 days, while the horse's OR of 55 and five-day turnaround are manageable factors for a horse racing in its natural role.
runners_data.comment: Mart has placed third two of his last six starts and brings strong recent consistency, running over today's trip and going — a genuine contender from stall one carrying 135 lb, though yet to score in this recent sequence.

runners_data.name: Rajeteriat
runners_data.note: Josephine Gordon partners this hold-up type returning after 46 days off for Chris Gordon — the 12 of 15 runners behind on similar going in the pace history is a concern, and all five historical runs in the sample came over 5f, leaving stamina for 6f at Brighton an open question.
runners_data.comment: Consistent placed efforts — third and second in his last three starts back and two starts back respectively — mark Rajeteriat as a genuine contender here, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; the concern is that last run 46 days ago and a winless recent run of form leave questions over whether he can finally convert.

runners_data.name: Big Time Rascal
runners_data.note: Two wins from ten runs on good ground and a consistent record at 6f for Simon Hodgson, but this is naturally a deep closer whose true style means it is at a positional disadvantage here — Benoit de la Sayette will need to find a more forward berth than the horse naturally prefers.
runners_data.comment: Big Time Rascal won two starts back but was fifth last time out, and while he has run over today's trip and going, that recent dip in form tempers confidence — 132 lb is no featherweight assignment for a horse rated 52.

runners_data.name: Manhattan Chute
runners_data.note: Won over this course and distance on good ground from a hold-up position, which is encouraging form, but the horse has finished outside the places in its last three starts and the 0/3 trainer-14 record adds caution; pushed into midfield here when its natural preference would be the rear.
runners_data.comment: Manhattan Chute returns on fair terms fitness-wise at 24 days, has run over today's trip and going, and that recent win catches the eye, but five defeats around it in his last six starts — including finishes of seventh and ninth — make him hard to fancy ranked sixth of seven on our figures.

runners_data.name: Bated Breeze
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on good ground at the last attempt and David Probert — one of the sharpest jockeys around — takes over for Gary & Josh Moore (1/19 in 14 days); the horse's genuine closing style means it needs something to go wrong for the front-runners, though Probert's ability to place a horse could compensate.
runners_data.comment: Bated Breeze bolsters his claims with a win last time out and has run over today's trip and going, while 129 lb is the factor to weigh against him.

runners_data.name: Kodi K
runners_data.note: Three-year-old on a mark of 47 for John Gallagher, carrying the least weight in the field at 123lbs and last seen finishing sixth over 6f on soft ground 38 days ago; a natural closer repositioned to midfield in this map, and the youngest, lightest horse in what looks a competitive sprint.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Kodi K is hard to fancy, though a second two starts back offers a crumb of encouragement; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 38 days off should leave him fresh.

races.paceDynamic: Mart is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner field and should lead comfortably from the gates, setting a sustainable rather than scorching gallop on Good to Firm ground over Brighton's undulating 6f. With no genuine pace pressure to trouble Mart, the tempo is likely to be controlled and honest rather than frenetic, meaning the race will be run to suit those who can travel close to the pace and produce a strong sustained finish rather than a late sprint from well off it. The field is heavily loaded with hold-up horses — Big Time Rascal, Manhattan Chute, Bated Breeze and Kodi K are all true hold-up types redistributed to midfield in this map because they cannot all settle at the back without gifting the race to Mart entirely. Dragon God and Rajeteriat are the natural hold-up runners most likely to actually occupy the rear positions. This race shape — a single uncontested leader on fast ground over an uphill finish — strongly favours horses that can sit prominently or in the first half of the field and sustain their effort to the line; genuine deep closers will need the pace to have been honest enough to reel Mart in, which is far from guaranteed given the lack of rivals to pressurise the leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mart Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Mart leads uncontested and sets a comfortable, controlled gallop that no rival is able to disrupt.
scenarios.body: Mart bounds clear from the gates and never faces a serious challenger for the lead, with the field strung out behind and chasing shadows from 2f out; horses with the ability to sit close in second or third and sustain a finish — rather than those making up ground from the rear — are the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Close-Up Pair Collar Leader
scenarios.trigger: If one or two of the redistributed hold-up types travels prominently and hits top gear to collar Mart inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A horse like Big Time Rascal or Bated Breeze, both of whom have won at 6f on good ground, finds a more prominent pitch than their natural style suggests and delivers a sustained challenge to overhaul a tiring Mart; the winner in this shape is a horse with strong 6f form on fast ground who gets a good position from the outset.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Reel Them In
scenarios.trigger: If Mart sets a stronger-than-expected pace that causes the front to collapse and the genuine closers arrive late.
scenarios.body: Dragon God or Rajeteriat, sitting at the back of the field in their natural positions, pick up the pieces as the pace takes its toll on those racing prominently; this scenario requires the gallop to be genuinely testing, which is unlikely but possible if Mart is pushed wider or harder than anticipated.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Blanket Finish Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is moderate and the whole field bunches, producing a messy scramble in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: With no real separation through the race, several hold-up horses find themselves in a position to challenge simultaneously; horses with sharp finishing speed and a jockey able to find a gap — such as Bated Breeze with David Probert — could steal a tight verdict in the melee.

watchPoints.text: Mart — watch the opening furlong; if Mart gets a clean break and no rival takes it on, the controlled gallop could turn this into a one-horse race that is very difficult to peg back on fast ground.

Big Time Rascal — Benoit de la Sayette's positioning in the opening stages is critical; if the horse gets shuffled back to its natural hold-up position, the uphill Brighton finish may simply not offer enough run to win from the rear.
Dragon God — raced over 5f in all recent runs and the step to 6f at Brighton, a track that rewards stamina, needs monitoring in running to see whether the horse is travelling or grinding early.

Rajeteriat — the 46-day absence combined with a form string showing limited recent action on comparable ground means any signs of greenness or ring-rustiness in the preliminaries would be an important early tell.

Bated Breeze — watch David Probert's positioning at the start; if he elects to push forward aggressively rather than drop the horse in, that signals intent and would represent a significant change of tactics worth noting.

races.name: Bet Responsibly With JenningsBet Handicap Stakes (Brighton Summer Sprint Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: King Cherry
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner whose entire chance pivots on uncontested lead-setting; Brighton 7f on fast ground suits a horse who can bowl along, but sim-going form reads 0W0P from five attempts and recent finishes of 7-5-6-8 over this trip suggest he tends to be headed before the line — the key question is whether a rare unopposed passage changes that.
runners_data.comment: Ranked top of our assessments among these seven, King Cherry has run over today's trip and going before and carries a workable 135 lb from stall 3; the concern is he's winless in his last five starts and returns just two days after his most recent outing.

runners_data.name: Solar Phoenix
runners_data.note: Returning from 55 days off for Roger Teal after a wind op (hood), so fitness is the immediate query; style is unclassified and his last start produced a distant tenth on good ground over a mile, though he has placed at 7f before and Dougie Costello's booking is an upgrade.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and yet to make the frame in recent efforts, Solar Phoenix does at least bring distance experience to this assignment; carrying 134 lb from stall six, however, with our rating suggesting he falls short of the top pair here, he faces a stiff task.

runners_data.name: Pennine Way
runners_data.note: Races prominently for Jack Channon and has the most realistic chance of latching on to King Cherry's heels; two runs on good ground at 7f produced a third and a seventh, form is inconsistent, but he freshened up 17 days ago and is the natural pressure point on the leader if he travels sweetly.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and lightly fit at 17 days, Pennine Way brings distance and going experience into this, and her rating of 61 offers a small edge — though she remains yet to win in her last five starts, stall two could at least ensure a clean break.

runners_data.name: Shes Got The Blues
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's filly arrives in excellent form with back-to-back wins on good ground over 7f, making her the standout on recent achievement; Myla Coppins claims 5lb and rides a hold-up style, which means she needs enough pace to have been set — the lean to front-running shapes slightly complicates her task, but her class edge is real.
runners_data.comment: Shes Got The Blues won back-to-back races before finishing third last time out, and she has experience over today's trip and going, making her a genuine threat carrying 130 lb from stall 5; the 41-day gap is the main query.

runners_data.name: Superstorm
runners_data.note: Consistent enough closer for Charlie Fellowes who has placed at 7f on good ground, though the visor goes on and the trainer is 0 from 12 in the last fortnight; needs a stronger gallop than this race is likely to produce and is outrated by Shes Got The Blues in a comparable style profile.
runners_data.comment: Superstorm has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 61 puts him firmly in contention from stall 7 with 23 days between runs suggesting he arrives fresh — the risk is he's winless in his last six starts, and the top pair must be overcome.

runners_data.name: Arvana Belle
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's filly is a genuine hold-up horse by inclination — her three placings include a third over 7f on good ground — but with Snow Day also naturally wanting to come from the rear, she is mapped to midfield, racing somewhat out of role; the blinkers (hood) may sharpen her early, but a STYLE_FIT of 0.93 flags the positional compromise.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a third two runs back the sole bright spot in a largely disappointing recent record, Arvana Belle at least has experience over today's distance and going and arrives on a quick 13-day turnaround, but ranked sixth of seven on our figures she faces a stiff task.

runners_data.name: Snow Day
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in the finish and carrying a poor recent string of 0-0-8-6-0; a natural hold-up horse pushed into a midfield mapping due to field composition, meaning her positional compromises compound already-thin form — the 5lb claim from Molly Gunn is the one mild positive in an otherwise difficult profile.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a string of unplaced efforts and our figures ranking her last of seven here, Snow Day faces a stiff ask — though she has run over today's trip before and a 38-day break could mean she returns fresher.

races.paceDynamic: King Cherry is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival prepared to contest the lead, should secure an uncontested bowl down Brighton's undulating 7f from the outset, setting a comfortable, controlled tempo on Good to Firm ground. Pennine Way will attempt to track from a prominent position, but with King Cherry dictating unchallenged, the sectionals are unlikely to be truly searching. The redistributed hold-up types — Snow Day and Arvana Belle — are genuine closers by inclination but are shown in midfield because the field's blend of styles prevents them from settling as far back as they would naturally wish, diluting their finish. This race shape strongly favours a front-runner or close-tracking prominent racer: a lone pace-setter controlling a modest gallop on fast ground at a track that already rewards those who settle handy and don't get caught wide on the long bend.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: King Cherry Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If King Cherry bowls off in front at a sustainable tempo and is never seriously pressured through the bend.
scenarios.body: King Cherry settles into an uncontested lead, regulates the fractions to suit himself, and the chasing pack never fully close the gap on the run to the line; Brighton's uphill finish and fast ground reward the horse who has conserved energy at the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Surges Late
scenarios.trigger: If King Cherry's early pace is faster than it appears and closer runners find the final two furlongs genuinely demanding, cracking the door open for a late finisher.
scenarios.body: Shes Got The Blues, who has two recent wins over 7f on good ground, is the likeliest beneficiary, producing a strong run from the rear as front-runners tire on the climb; this shape requires the gallop to have been hot enough to cause genuine attrition, which is less likely given the lone-leader setup.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Overpowers
scenarios.trigger: If King Cherry shows any sign of stopping or is collared turning for home, allowing a prominent tracker to pounce.
scenarios.body: Pennine Way, lobbing just off the pace in second or third, could pick up the pieces if the leader weakens; Solar Phoenix, whose style is uncertain but who may also race handily, offers secondary interest in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If King Cherry sets an unexpectedly strong pace and fades sharply, scrambling the finish order.
scenarios.body: A chaotic final furlong would theoretically benefit the closers, but Snow Day carries a fade-in-finish flag and poor recent form, and Arvana Belle is racing out of her natural deep hold-up role here, limiting the reliability of either to deliver in a late-surge scenario.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether King Cherry gets a clean break from the stalls — if he misses the kick, the entire pace dynamic collapses and Pennine Way may inherit the lead at a faster gallop than expected.

Shes Got The Blues is the form pick but relies on Myla Coppins (5lb claimer) delivering a precise hold-up ride in a race that may not generate enough early fractions — monitor how far back she settles leaving the stalls.

Solar Phoenix is 55 days absent and has had wind surgery; if he arrives short of peak fitness his uncertain racing style could see him dropped out early and never competitive, distorting the midfield picture.

Arvana Belle and Snow Day are both true closers compressed into midfield — if they end up racing keenly trying to find a position, energy burned early will blunt any finish they might otherwise produce.

Brighton's 7f starts on a slight rise before the downhill sweep into the home straight — King Cherry's ability to relax on that opening climb rather than over-race will determine whether this is a true contest or a procession.

races.name: Al Nujaifi Racing Series Fillies & Mares Conditions Stakes - Arab Race

runners_data.name: Fareedhat El Izz (A)
runners_data.comment: Fareedhat El Izz is lightly raced and open to plenty of improvement, with two wins in her last four starts — most recently a victory — and she steps back out after 41 days carrying 133 lb from stall 3.

runners_data.name: Victoria (A)
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced and open to plenty of improvement, Victoria (A) showed her best last time out with a win, and a second two starts back suggests consistency is building — unexposed at this level with more to offer.

runners_data.name: Anafah (A)
runners_data.comment: Anafah is lightly raced and unexposed, yet her recent starts have been frustrating — four consecutive ninths in her last four outings, with a fourth five starts back her best recent showing. Returning after 153 days off, she has it all to prove here.

runners_data.name: Pharitz Lahia (A)
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts but placed second two starts back and third three starts back, Pharitz Lahia arrives 32 days fresh, carrying 130 lb from stall 4 — still unexposed and open to improvement.

runners_data.name: Ghayah (A)
runners_data.comment: Ghayah is unexposed and open to improvement; she was second last time out and has shown fair form in recent starts, yet to win in her last three. Returning after 22 days, she carries 129 lb from stall one.
